newsitem.title: SPAIN: Opera says to invest over 500bln pta in Retevision.
newsitem.headline: Opera says to invest over 500bln pta in Retevision.

text.p: The Opera consortium, comprised of Banco Central Hispano, France Telecom and Sprint said late on Tuesday it would invest more than 500 billion pesetas in a Spanish digital network and the development of the telephone business if it wins the auction for 60 percent of Retevision.
In a statement, Opera added that its plans for Retevision, which will become Spain's second basic telephone operator, included the creation of 6,000 jobs.

On Tuesday, Retevision announced that the rival Endesa -Stet group offer was 116.36 billion pesetas ($805.1 million) while Opera had offered just 84 billion pesetas ($578.5 million) for the initial privatisation.

Under the terms of the auction, 40 percent of the weighting goes to the highest bidder, with 20 percent for infrastructure and networks, 20 percent for financial backing and strategic plan, 10 percent for experience and 10 percent for service improvement and benefit to the Spanish economy.

The Spanish government now has two months to designate the winner of the auction, but the final result of the auction could be known in as little as two weeks, Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado said on Tuesday.
